PullRequest.Title: sessions: align Connected headers and Changes card spacing
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #341558. Follow-up to #341337.

Balance the space around the Branch Changes dropdown without shrinking the control, and align single-row Connected tab headers with neighboring panel headers.

## Changes

- Remove the first diff card's extra top gutter only inside the Sessions Changes editor, preserving its normal/sticky flow height so the diff body does not jump when scrolling. Later card gaps, flat file headers, and other multi-diff editors retain their existing styling.
- Use 32px single-row Connected tab strips (28px compact), including when wrapping is enabled but all tabs fit on one row. The active cap remains flush with the panel top; actual wrapped rows and upper pinned rows keep their existing geometry.
- Center inactive single-row pill fills on their labels and actions, including resting selected, dirty, and pinned tabs.
- Cover the toolbar/content boundary and row-height behavior with focused regression tests and header fixtures. The dropdown's height, text, and icon sizing are unchanged.

## Testing

1. In an Agents window, open Changes with `multiDiffEditor.experimental.variant` set to `cards`. At the top of the editor, compare the gap above the Branch Changes control with the gap below it to the first card. Confirm later cards retain their gaps, then scroll and collapse/expand the first card to check its sticky header.
2. Switch the variant to `noCards`; confirm flat headers and the dropdown size are unchanged.
3. Use Connected tabs with default and compact tab heights. With wrapping off, then on with all tabs fitting, confirm the tab-strip baseline aligns with neighboring headers and the active tab has no top inset.
4. Narrow the pane until tabs actually wrap. Confirm upper pill rows and the connected bottom row retain their sizing, and Add Tab and editor actions remain usable. Repeat with separate pinned rows, RTL, and high-contrast themes. Check Pill and legacy tabs as negative cases.

- `npm run compile` — passed, including client type checking and extension/media builds.

- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/test/browser/sessionChangesEditor.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/test/browser/editor.contribution.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/editorPart.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts` — passed (206 tests).
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/browser/media/sessionChangesEditor.css src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/media/editorPart.css src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/browser/media/connectedEditorTabs.css` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/test/browser/sessionChangesEditor.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/test/browser/editor.contribution.test.ts src/vs/sessions/test/browser/editorPart.test.ts src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## Visual comparison

Native Code OSS, default density, card-based Changes editor, with icon fonts loaded. Each theme's pair uses the same content, pane width, zoom, and crop; the baseline restores the old 29px strip height and first-card margin in the same running window. The dropdown's dimensions are unchanged within every pair, and later card gaps remain 4px.

The active theme IDs were verified as `Light 2026`, `Dark 2026`, and `Default High Contrast Light`. Native scrolling checks keep the first card's header flow height and diff-body offset at 36px across the sticky transition; inactive labels are centered on their painted fills.

The CSS regression tests cover all four theme types; the separate header fixture comparisons also cover default and compact sizing. Use the PR's Screenshots & Tests report for the fixture theme sweep.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and scroll the Sessions Changes editor in card mode, including collapsing or expanding the leading diff
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The multi-diff widget renders its existing diff entries, then CSS computes the leading header's margin and height. On sticky transitions the existing shadow class changes selector matching; no changed JavaScript or asynchronous operation must complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible diff cards; the new selector matches only the single entry carrying first-diff-entry, so changed work remains O(1) even when the change list is large.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser style/layout on the UI thread; no queue, limiter, IPC, or parallel operation is introduced. Sticky state changes remain handled by the existing widget path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Cold and warm rendering use the same CSS rule, with no cache key, miss, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the diff is CSS-only on this product path, the first-entry class is assigned by the existing item autorun, and no changed event handler or geometry read was added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style recalculation duration varies with DOM size, but the changed selector targets one header and preserves the same 36px flow height, so it does not establish additional scaling work or layout churn.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change replaces the first card's 4px top margin with 4px of content height, preserving total flow geometry across normal and sticky states rather than adding repeated layout work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Lay out Connected editor tabs during editor opening, resizing, tab-option changes, and transitions between single-row and wrapped layouts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing MultiEditorTabsControl layout writes wrapping and row classes, reads tab offsets, computes control height, and may request one group relayout when the resulting height changes. The diff changes only CSS row-height and inactive-fill inset values consumed by that existing pass.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible editor-tab count. Existing layout already iterates and measures the tabs; the diff neither adds a per-tab operation nor increases iteration count, and selector matching remains linear in the same tab collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM writes and measurements are synchronously serialized in the existing UI layout pass. No added scheduling, burst, queue, or concurrency exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The control continues caching its used dimensions and only relayouts the group when computed height differs. The diff does not alter cache keys, invalidation, miss behavior, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: source tracing shows wrapping detection, per-tab measurements, computeHeight, and relayout behavior are unchanged; only fixed CSS calculations and test expectations changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The strip is 3-7px taller depending on prior host and density, so painting covers slightly more area, but this is a bounded intentional geometry change and there is no evidence of extra layout passes, dropped frames, or scaling amplification.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The intended fixed-height increase does not add synchronous measurement, force a new read-after-write cycle, or amplify work with tab cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and horizontally scroll the Sessions chat composite tab bar using the shared modern-ui-editor-tab-strip selector
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added selector gives the existing chat strip the new fixed row height. Its existing ResizeObserver reports a stable height change and existing scroll handlers update clipping; no new callback, geometry read, or extra reveal operation is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chat tabs and resize/scroll event frequency. Existing clipping and scrolling work retain their prior cardinality; the CSS rule is inherited once at the strip and does not add per-event JavaScript.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ResizeObserver callbacks and scroll handlers run on the UI event loop as before. The fixed CSS height can produce one observer notification when applied, not an unbounded observer loop or concurrent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No data cache is involved. Scroll dimensions and observed height continue to be maintained by the existing observers, with unchanged invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the only product use of modern-ui-editor-tab-strip is the chat composite bar, and its observer, scroll, clipping, and layout code is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact paint cost depends on viewport width and theme, but the height increase is bounded and no changed mechanism repeats it per frame or per tab.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The broader selector intentionally aligns this single strip and adds no repeated synchronous work or lifecycle retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the added and updated browser regression tests and visual fixtures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test setup creates bounded synthetic DOM trees and performs geometry assertions; this code is not loaded on product startup or interaction paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed test matrices over themes, densities, widths, and a small bounded number of tabs/cards.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tests execute their awaited layouts serially under the existing browser test runner; no product concurrency behavior changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No product cache behavior is affected; test-local DOM is created and disposed per suite.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: all changed TypeScript outside fixtures is under test/browser paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Test runtime may increase modestly from additional matrix cases, but it does not affect end-user performance and is not a product regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable product performance regression; the additional work is test-only and bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and every diff page. Traced the Sessions Changes card, Connected editor-tab layout, and chat composite strip through their style/layout ownership. The PR changes bounded CSS geometry and tests only; it introduces no extra expensive boundary, repeated measurement pass, retained lifecycle state, cache regression, or concurrency fan-out, so no finding was submitted.
